preview.overview: BYU brings the College Football Belt to LaVell Edwards Stadium to face Cincinnati in a matchup that will crown a new champion if the Bearcats can pull off an upset. The belt has been held by the Cougars since they beat UCF 39-31, and Cincinnati will need to break through on the road to claim it.
key_matchups: BYU's ability to protect the ball after scoring 31 and 28 points in their last two wins versus Cincinnati's defense that held Colorado to 35 and Texas Tech to 24
Cincinnati's offensive consistency on the road, where they've struggled significantly (losses to Iowa State, Houston, and Utah) compared to their home performance
BYU's resilience following back-to-back losses to Utah and UCF versus Cincinnati's need to string together consecutive wins
preview.betting_angles: BYU owns a 4-0 all-time series advantage and has won the last two meetings convincingly, including a 26-14 victory just last year. Cincinnati has shown serious road struggles, losing three of their last four away games while BYU has demonstrated the ability to win close contests at home (31-29 vs Kansas, 27-20 vs Arizona State). The Bearcats' recent form is inconsistent with two wins sandwiched around three losses, while BYU has shown more stability despite their recent setbacks.
preview.prediction_writeup: BYU's home-field advantage and clear historical dominance over Cincinnati make the Cougars the logical choice to retain the belt. The Bearcats have been plagued by road inconsistency, losing decisively at Iowa State (13-41) and Houston (24-31), and Cincinnati hasn't shown the offensive firepower to keep pace with BYU's recent scoring outputs. While BYU stumbled against Utah and UCF, their ability to win tight games at home and their 4-0 series record against Cincinnati suggests they'll find a way to execute when the belt is on the line. Cincinnati's defense has had moments but will face a BYU offense that put up 31 and 28 points in their last two victories.
